served.stem: Approximately what percentage of the sodium filtered at the glomerulus is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule?
served.bankWhy: The nephron reabsorbs sodium in a predictable order, and the proximal convoluted tubule is the workhorse. It reclaims about two thirds of the filtered sodium, with water and much else following along, then the thick ascending limb takes roughly a quarter and the distal tubule and collecting duct fine tune the last few percent. The choice sitting near two thirds matches that bulk reabsorption role.

answer.line: The proximal tubule is the workhorse. It reclaims about two thirds of the filtered sodium, with water following.

steps: Picture the filtered sodium as a budget the nephron spends, segment by segment.
The proximal tubule spends most of it: about two thirds, with water following.
Then the thick ascending limb takes about a quarter, and the distal tubule and collecting duct fine-tune the last few percent.

choices.note: About a quarter is the thick ascending limb, the second-largest site. It is a real share, just for the next segment down.
Just under half undersells the proximal tubule. Its brush border and dense mitochondria let it reclaim about two thirds before the loop.
About 5 percent is the distal tubule, the fine-tuning end of the nephron, not the bulk.
About two thirds of the filtered sodium, in the first segment.
Nearly all filtered sodium is reclaimed across the whole nephron. The stem asks about one segment, the proximal tubule.
